open_questions: `_make_scratch_git_repo()`'s return shape has a real textual tension in the spec: design point (3) says the helper mirrors the test fixture and should 'return the repo path' (singular, Path only, matching tests/controller/test_loop_run.py::git_repo which returns only `repo_dir: Path`), but AC-4's own wording says the unit test 'asserts a real HEAD sha is returned from a real ... git repo' -- which reads as if `_make_scratch_git_repo()` itself returns the sha (or a (Path, str) tuple), not just the Path. Unlike AC-1/AC-2/AC-3/AC-13, AC-4 carries no adversarial-review 'CORRECTED' tag flagging this as a known/resolved wording issue, so it may be a genuine latent ambiguity rather than something already vetted. My plan (Step 4) resolves this by precedent -- `_make_scratch_git_repo(workspace_root) -> Path` returns only the Path (matching design point 3's explicit text and the fixture it mirrors), with a separate companion `_head_sha(repo) -> str` helper (mirroring the test file's own separate `_head_sha` function) providing the sha AC-4's test asserts on. This is a grounded, precedent-based resolution, not an invented one, but a plan-auditor/fixer should confirm this reading against the spec author's intent before treating AC-4 as satisfied by a 2-function split rather than a single dual-return function.

The spec's design point 3 and the AC-4 test both assume `compute_candidate_tree_sha` (imported in the new test file from `controller.main_loop`) is exercised directly, standalone, outside `run_one_candidate_pass` -- confirmed straightforward from reading `controller/main_loop.py`'s actual signature (`compute_candidate_tree_sha(handoff, repo, candidate_target_path, base_sha)`), so this is not flagged as blocking, but noting it here since the AC text describes it only in prose ('succeeds when called standalone against that repo + a scratch candidate file + candidate_target_path + the captured bootstrap_commit_sha as base_sha') without naming the exact `CandidateHandoff` construction the test needs -- Step 9's test must construct a `CandidateHandoff(path=<scratch file>, content_sha256=<any value>)` itself; this is a mechanical, non-design-decision detail already fully determined by `CandidateHandoff`'s existing dataclass shape (imported from `controller.dispatch`), so no design judgment was needed to resolve it, but flagging it in case the plan-auditor wants to double-check the exact handoff-construction shape used in the test.
